findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph tile in place of a picture of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical wrench icon in a 96px pale-green square. It occupies the thumbnail slot but carries no information about which tool it is, so it reads as a placeholder left on show.
findings.impact: Members recognise tools by look ('the drill with two batteries'); a repeated stand-in may slow scanning and makes the page look unfinished, which lowers trust in a volunteer-run service.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail slot is for: real photographs of the library's own stock, or a tool-specific drawn glyph per category; otherwise remove the slot rather than show a stand-in.

findings.title: No signature or identity floor: the design could belong to any reservation service
findings.description: Identity is only 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body text with a stock wrench glyph. The product's distinctive constraint (a few opening sessions a week, one of each tool) is rendered with a stock calendar and radio cards. Nothing from the library's world (the membership card the green is said to come from, the room, the desk, the community centre) appears visually.
findings.impact: The 'neighbourly' attribute is carried only by copy; members may not recognise this as their local library's own service, and the page offers nothing memorable.
findings.recommendation: Decide one signature taken from the library's own mechanism or material (for example how sessions or the membership card are shown) and an identity floor (a designed name mark) that 'neighbourly, not folksy' can be read from, within Operate conventions.

findings.title: At 375 px tool names truncate with an ellipsis and badges strand 'Oct' on its own line
findings.description: Card titles are cut to 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' so the two-battery and one-battery drills look identical; 'Available from Sat 10 / Oct' wraps leaving one word; nav links wrap to two lines each.
findings.impact: On phones, the main device, members may open the wrong drill; the stranded words look careless, against 'careful, not fussy'.
findings.recommendation: Decide how card content reflows at narrow widths so full tool names and badge text fit (wrapping, not truncation).

findings.title: On phones the search form sits below all ten tool cards
findings.description: At 1280 the search bar is above the list; at 375 it moves to after the last card, just before Opening times.
findings.impact: The find page's entry point is out of view on the main device; members who know the tool they want may have to scroll past every card to search.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same source and visual order at every width so search precedes results.

findings.title: Tool details list has two different value-column offsets
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x≈224 while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x≈180, so one list reads as two misaligned tables.
findings.impact: Visible misalignment in the one place members compare specs undermines 'careful'.
findings.recommendation: Render the details as one aligned list.

findings.title: Basket session cards: one full-width orphan above five cramped cards
findings.description: At 1280 the six sessions lay out as one full-width card (Wednesday 28 October) followed by a row of five narrow cards, each label wrapping to three lines; sessions run latest-first.
findings.impact: The orphan card looks emphasised though it is the furthest session; three-line wraps and reverse order may make the nearest session harder to find.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list that holds equal items at every width, in date order.

findings.title: Filter panel uses a browser-default date input showing 'yyyy/mm/dd'
findings.description: The 'Available from' field is a native date control with a year-first placeholder and the category is a native select whose label baseline sits lower than the date label.
findings.impact: Year-first format conflicts with the declared en-GB 'Saturday 17 October' format and the unthemed control reads as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the date filter presents dates in the member's format, consistent with the session calendar.

findings.title: Dark theme: available badges lose their tint while later-date badges keep a fill
findings.description: In dark mode the green 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges show no visible background, while grey 'Available from Sat 17 Oct' badges keep a filled chip, inverting which state looks emphasised.
findings.impact: Many members use dark mode in the evening; the available-now state looks weaker than the not-yet state.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge pair so the available state keeps the stronger treatment.

findings.title: Confirm and done leave the right half of wide screens empty, and the footer stops short
findings.description: Forms and the 'What happens next' box stop at ~700px inside a 1088px container while summary boxes span full width; on short pages the white footer ends above an unfilled grey band.
findings.impact: Mixed widths with no relation to each other and bands that stop short make the final steps look unfinished at desktop widths.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content measure for these pages and keep the page ground continuous to the bottom.
